A_target.statement:
The [[Definition:Volume|volume]] of a [[Definition:Ball|ball]] of radius $r$ is:
:$\dfrac 4 3 \pi r^3$

B_source.statement: If two solids have cross-sections of equal area at every height, then they have equal volume.

substitutions.the two solids: a hemisphere, and a cylinder with a cone removed

derived.equal cross-sections: the hemisphere volume equals cylinder minus cone

object_map.reformulation: Compare a hemisphere with a cylinder from which a cone with apex at the base center has been removed.

validity_conditions: The cone must have its apex at the center of the base, so that its cross-section at height h has radius h.
The volumes of the cylinder and cone are taken as known.
proof_plan: The cross-section of a hemisphere of radius $r$ at height $h$ is a disk of area $\pi \paren {r^2 - h^2}$.

Take a cylinder of radius $r$ and height $r$, and remove a cone with apex at the center of its base and base its top face.
At height $h$ the cross-section is an annulus of area $\pi r^2 - \pi h^2$.
By [[Cavalieri's Principle]], the hemisphere has volume $\pi r^3 - \dfrac 1 3 \pi r^3 = \dfrac 2 3 \pi r^3$.

Doubling, the ball has volume $\dfrac 4 3 \pi r^3$.
{{qed}}
